newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Gold-Broker sees gold floor price.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Gold-Broker sees gold floor price.

text.p: A "cautious reversal of sentiment" has emerged now that the floor price in gold has been reached, for the time being at least, Australian brokers JB Were and Son Ltd said on Tuesday.
"We are looking for gold to consolidate in the US$345-$360 an ounce range in coming weeks," Were said in a report.
The view is supported by local bullion dealers who see little drive among investors to move the price much either way.
COMEX April gold settled US$2.60 lower on Monday at US$350.40 an ounce. COMEX gold volume was estimated at a modest 40,000 lots.
"Better control over inflation in most economies and buoyant equity markets are depriving gold of a place in investment portfolios," Were said.
Dealers noted the overnight slip in the gold price was likely to discourage much interest among Australian producers to unwind forward positions.
On the contrary, if anything hedging among miners is on the rise.
"Jittery producers have continued to sell forward at any opportunity," Were said.
The move to boost forward sales is also based on uncertainties in the future value of the Australian dollar against the U.S. greenback.
A strong Australian dollar has battered the Australian-denominated gold price, which hasn't traded at such low levels since the 1980s.
The Perth Mint on Tuesday quoted spot gold at U$350.33/A$443.68 an ounce.
For miners watching the value of their gold deteriorate, the ability to lock into the foreign currency markets is proving as difficult as predicting the gold price.

"There is no consensus amongst economists about the direction of the Australian dollar," said the International Banks and Securities Association of Australia, after polling Australian economists for a survey. "The Australian dollar-U.S. dollar forecast values over a six month horizon range from 74 Australian cents to 82 Australian cents."
There is a growing expectation that U.S. Federal Reserve Board will hike the federal funds rate by 25 basis points when it meets later on Tuesday.
Such a move might hobble the Australian dollar somewhat, causing the Australian-dollar gold price to go up.
"Although, this hasn't been the case yet, the potential exisits to sink the Aussie (dollar) to give locals a bit of a price increase," one bullion dealer said.
However, any gains could be offset by a tandem decline in the U.S. dollar-gold price, the dealer added.
